title: Adopt the Register design system across public human projections
objective: Replace Epistemedia's oversized, card-heavy forensic shell with a compact, human-readable public design system derived from the owner-approved Register template at yoheinakajima/register commit 5ac05e2758885d92ed2a9a8cfd4c6eb70ccbdbe4. Apply one coherent hierarchy across every deterministically generated HTML surface while preserving accepted evidence, policy-relative readings, machine-readable twins, public identities, and contribution semantics.
required_evaluation: exact source review of the Register DESIGN.md contract, register.css grammar, representative dossier and program examples, and responsive behavior at owner-approved source commit 5ac05e2758885d92ed2a9a8cfd4c6eb70ccbdbe4

design-token and component mapping that adopts Register's compact sans hierarchy, monospace identity layer, hairline alignment, restrained surfaces, state semantics, and no-JavaScript degradation without importing sample claims or changing Epistemedia's evidence model

representative desktop and 390 px visual review of the homepage, How We Know library, Cases 001-004, About, For agents, Open Dockets, Explore, a topic projection, an object page, status, documentation, and review or projection receipts

accessibility review covering semantic headings, skip link, keyboard-visible focus, native details and summary behavior, link affordance, contrast, readable line length, reduced motion, and absence of horizontal page overflow except explicitly scrollable technical tables or code

human-readable substrate review confirming that object kind and stable identity are subordinate to title and summary, related-object links remain available, and technical identifiers wrap safely rather than competing with prose

HTML, Markdown, JSON, llms.txt, sitemap, local REST, MCP, and CLI parity; accepted dossier, source-span, relation, count, evaluation, review-receipt, open-docket, and mission bytes and meanings remain unchanged
license and provenance review for any substantial Register-derived stylesheet material, retaining the Register MIT copyright and permission notice where required
deterministic make check, clean tracked state, generated-output comparison, disclosure audit, exact path-scope audit, and fresh-clone exact-head independent review
protected merge, resulting-main validation, separately authorized Pages deployment, and live custom-domain release-identity plus representative-route read-back before claiming the redesign is live
acceptance: all generated human HTML surfaces use one shared Register-derived visual grammar and remain complete without JavaScript
headlines are compact and sans-serif, prose remains comfortably readable, identifiers and metadata use a visibly smaller monospace layer, and no routine page relies on oversized hero text
hierarchy comes primarily from alignment, whitespace, and hairlines; routine cards have no blurred shadow, decorative gradient, rounded container, colored edge stripe, or ornamental background grid

topic and object projections render as readable register rows or equivalent aligned records with inspectable interlinks and collapsed technical identity rather than equal-weight HTML bullet dumps or dense card walls
numbers and states retain explicit labels, source or receipt context, and non-color cues; every displayed total remains derived from typed members
representative pages have one H1, no scripts, visible keyboard focus, no page-level horizontal overflow at 390 px, and stable canonical and twin links
accepted Cases 001-004, mission, reviewed open dockets, policies, evidence records, public IDs, and machine-readable representations remain semantically unchanged
full deterministic validation and an exact-head independent review pass before protected integration
limitations: This task changes visual presentation, shared HTML chrome, and accessibility-oriented markup only; it does not change evidence, conclusions, policies, schemas, protocol semantics, governance authority, admission rules, or contribution automation.
Register is a design source, not an epistemic source. Its sample content, sample identifiers, navigation destinations, and example numbers are not imported into Epistemedia.
A visual resemblance to Register is not sufficient: the implementation must preserve Epistemedia's existing content density, exact twins, interlinks, and disclosure-safe deterministic compilation.

The public npm package design-slop-cop was unavailable during the source-template audit. Its 0/14 score may not be claimed unless the package becomes available; every explicit DESIGN.md requirement must instead be checked through the enumerated fallback checklist in the EM-0043 execution plan, and the bounded tooling gap must remain recorded.

No research provider call, evidence admission, case creation, policy change, constitution change, credential or account action, spend, DNS change, merge, publication, or deployment is authorized merely by registering this task; protected integration and deployment retain their normal gates.
